_description: A USB data-line protector on a 30 x 15 mm two-layer board: J1 (4-pin header in), U1 (ESDA6V1BC6, a four-channel TVS array: the KiCad library's own symbol and SOT-23-6 footprint), J2 (4-pin header out). Both headers carry D+, GND, D-, VBUS on pins 1-4; each data line flows through U1, D+ in on pin 1 and out on pin 6, D- on 3 and 4, a TVS channel to ground at each, and both COM pins (2 and 5), which the part joins inside, are on GND. Tracks 0.25 mm on KiCad's default rules. It passes kicad-cli pcb drc at every severity with nothing unconnected, carries the library's pin names on every pad, and runs VBUS and GND at 0.5 A. Its schematic, esd_guard.kicad_sch, is the same circuit on KiCad's stock symbols, every footprint on the board linked to its symbol: it passes kicad-cli sch erc at every severity and matches the board exactly. The project's own sym-lib-table and fp-lib-table name the stock libraries, so ERC reads the same on a host whose KiCad was never configured. selftest/assets/make_baseline.py made all of it, and says how. vbus_droop.cir models the VBUS path from the host through the cable and the board to J2 under a 0.5 A step, and dips to 4.83 V against USB 2.0's 4.75 V. esd_guard.kicad_dru holds one custom rule (usb_pair: the data pair at least 0.2 mm wide), which the 0.25 mm tracks keep and pcb.drc's probes show live; esd_guard.symbols.json is the statement pcb.schematic_from_board writes the same circuit from. esda6v1bc6_land.json is ST's recommended SOT23-6L land, numbered by function, which KiCad's SOT-23-6 fits to 0.0125 mm. lipo_charger.kicad_pcb (make_power_board.py) is a second board, placed and netted but not routed, that only the three LiPo rules read: an MCP73833 charger with its THERM on an NTC, an MF-MSMF075 between the cell and a 28 AWG wire, and an AP9101CK cutoff sensing the cell through 330 ohm. enclosure.step is a closed 2 mm box around the populated board, its lid 2.365 mm over the header pins; the footprints' 3D models are KiCad's own, kept in selftest/assets/3d/ so the fit sees the same parts on every host.

pcb_cell.source: the baseline's cell: a 1-cell LiPo whose datasheet gives a 2.75 V discharge cut-off, with no protection circuit of its own (pcm_cutoff_min_v null). A sealed fixture value, not a product's.

pcb_charger.source: Microchip MCP73833/4 datasheet (DS22005): THERM is pin 8 of the MSOP-10 (KiCad's MCP73833-xxx-UN symbol, read), and the part has a safety timer that ends a charge that never finishes (recalled from DS22005; re-read it before relying on it)

pcb_fuse.source: Bourns MF-MSMF series datasheet (REV. BE): MF-MSMF075, maximum time to trip 0.2 s at 8.0 A

pcb_conductor.source: 28 AWG solid copper, 0.0810 mm^2 (ASTM B258), PVC insulated: 70 C in service, 160 C its short-circuit limit (IEC 60364-5-54's k = 115 pair)

pcb_cutoffs.source: Diodes Inc. AP9101C datasheet: VDD is pin 2 of SOT-23-5 (KiCad's AP9101CK symbol, read); a variant with a 2.90 V overdischarge detection voltage at +-50 mV, so 2.85 V at the least (recalled; re-read the option table before relying on it)

_notes._units: Millimetres for every length (KiCad's file unit), amperes, degrees C of rise above ambient, ounces of copper per square foot (1 oz = 35 um = 1.378 mil).
_notes._paths: pcb_board, pcb_spice_deck and pcb_enclosure_step resolve against the PROJECT ROOT (ctx.root). Its project file (.kicad_pro), custom rules (.kicad_dru) and schematic (.kicad_sch, with every sheet under it) when they exist beside it with the same name, and the project's sym-lib-table and fp-lib-table, go with it to kicad-cli: they hold the design rules, KiCad's ERC and DRC exclusions and the libraries.
_notes.pcb_board: The board this pack checks. One board per project projection; a project with two boards scopes the key (pcb.pcb_board) per model, or runs two projects.
_notes.pcb_net_currents_a: {net: amperes} for every net whose current matters. pcb.net_width judges only the nets named here, because the board does not say what flows where. 0.5 A on VBUS and GND is a USB 2.0 port's budget.
_notes.pcb_temp_rise_limit_c: How far above ambient a track may run, degrees C. 10 C is the common design choice and the bottom of IPC-2221's fitted range (10-100 C): below it the formula is extrapolation, and the verdict says so.
_notes.pcb_copper_oz_outer: Copper weight of the outer layers. 1 oz is what a fab quotes without being asked; the gate uses that and says '[pack default]' when this key is absent.
_notes.pcb_copper_oz_inner: Copper weight of inner layers, 0.5 oz by the same convention. Unused on this two-layer board.
_notes.pcb_drc_severity: all (the default), error or warning. 'all' because a check at error severity cannot see a warning, and the fab still prints the silk a warning is about. Waive a finding by excluding it in KiCad, which records it in the .kicad_pro: never by narrowing this.
_notes.pcb_drc_timeout_s: Wall clock for one kicad-cli run. This board takes well under a second, a 4-layer board of about a hundred footprints about 2 s; 120 s is for a hang, which reads as a skip.
_notes.pcb_erc_severity: all (the default), error or warning, for pcb.erc, by the same reasoning as pcb_drc_severity. The schematic is the board's name with .kicad_sch (KiCad's rule for a project's root schematic) unless pcb_schematic names another for ERC; pcb.parity always compares with the board's own, as KiCad does.
_notes.pcb_fab: The fab whose published limits pcb.fab_rules holds the board to: jlcpcb (gates/fab/jlcpcb.json, each number quoted from its capability page with the day it was read), or a path from the project root to a fab file of the same shape. The row is chosen by the board's copper layer count and pcb_copper_oz_outer.
_notes.pcb_spice_deck: The SPICE deck pcb.spice runs with ngspice -b, from the project root. The deck is the project's model of the circuit, not the board: ngspice solves what it says. Relative .include and .lib paths resolve from the deck's directory.
_notes.pcb_spice_measure: The .meas result the verdict reads (ngspice lowercases names; so does the gate).
_notes.pcb_spice_min: The lowest value that passes, in pcb_spice_units. 4.75 V is USB 2.0's minimum VBUS at a high-power port's device connector. pcb_spice_max is the highest; give either or both.
_notes.pcb_spice_units: The measure's units, as ngspice computes it (SI: V, A, s). Stated by the project, because the gate cannot tell which quantity a .meas measures.
_notes.pcb_spice_timeout_s: Wall clock for one ngspice run. The baseline deck solves in about 0.01 s.
_notes.pcb_enclosure_step: The enclosure's solid (its walls and lid, the material, not the cavity) as a STEP file in mm, from the project root. The baseline's is a closed box made by selftest/assets/make_enclosure.py around the populated baseline board.
_notes.pcb_board_placement: Where the board sits in the enclosure's frame: turned rot_z_deg about z, then moved by x, y, z mm. The board's own frame is kicad-cli's STEP export with --user-origin 0x0mm: the board file's (0, 0) at the origin, x right, y up (KiCad's y negated), z up from the board's bottom face.
_notes.pcb_enclosure_clearance_mm: The smallest gap any part may keep from the enclosure. 1 mm is a common allowance for print and assembly tolerance; the board body itself may touch (it sits on standoffs). The baseline's nearest part, a header, is 2.365 mm under the lid.
_notes.pcb_enclosure_bodiless: References of placed parts that have no body to fit (an antenna drawn in copper): each listed is a statement that the fit need not see it. Every other SMD or through-hole part must name a 3D model that kicad-cli finds, or pcb.enclosure_fit skips.
_notes.pcb_fit_timeout_s: Wall clock for the STEP export and for the geometry, each. The baseline takes about 1 s and 3 s.
_notes.pcb_pin_names_ignore: Pin names pcb.pin_names never compares: unused-pin names, which may sit on any net, and KiCad's hidden-name placeholder. Every other repeated name must carry one net.
_notes.pcb_land_drawings: {ref: drawing record} for pcb.land_pattern, each a JSON file from the project root: {part, source, view: "top", y_axis: "up" (as printed) or "down" (as a KiCad footprint), pads: [{number, function, x, y, w, h}]} in mm. The baseline holds U1 to ST's recommended SOT23-6L land; KiCad's SOT-23-6 fits it to 0.0125 mm.
_notes.pcb_cell: The cell the power rules protect: its connector's ref, value and positive pin on the board named by board (else pcb_board), min_v (the datasheet's lowest discharge voltage) and pcm_cutoff_min_v (the lowest voltage the cell's own protection circuit opens at, null for none). The baseline's power records name lipo_charger.kicad_pcb, a board only these three tier-0 rules read.
_notes.pcb_charger: The charger: ref, value, thermistor_pin (its THERM pin, null when the part has none), ntc_ref (the NTC wired to it) and safety_timer (JSON true or false: whether the datasheet gives the part a charge timer). pcb.charge_protection.
_notes.pcb_fuse: The fuse in the cell path: ref, value and trip_max_s, the datasheet's guaranteed [amperes, maximum seconds to trip] points. pcb.fuse_conductor judges each.
_notes.pcb_conductor: The conductor the fuse protects: ref, value, pins (all on the net the fuse feeds), area_mm2 of ONE conductor (parallel contacts get no credit), start_c (its temperature in service) and limit_c (what its insulation or rating allows in a fault). The verdict turns on limit_c: say where it comes from.
_notes.pcb_cutoffs: The parts that cut the cell off: [{ref, value, sense_pin, series_ref (the one two-pad part between the cell's net and the sense pin, such as the datasheet's series resistor on VDD; null when the sense pin sits on the cell's net), threshold_min_v (the datasheet's lowest detection voltage), source}]. An empty list is a statement that there are none.
